projects.title: E-invoicing Copilot
projects.summary: Reads a company's invoice export and reports, invoice by invoice, what would stop each one being sent as a UAE e-invoice.
projects.statusNote: The validator is built and tested against a fictional sample dataset. It checks the Ministry of Finance mandatory fields. The full PINT-AE schema rules are not checked yet.
projects.roleNote: Design and build of the validator and its report.
overview: The UAE is introducing mandatory e-invoicing in the PINT-AE format. Most businesses do not know whether the invoices their accounting system produces today would pass. This tool answers that from an export.

It reads a CSV or Excel export, checks every invoice against the Ministry of Finance mandatory-fields document, and writes a readiness report and a findings file: which invoices are ready, which are blocked, and what to fix first.

Each rule is tagged by how certain it is: stated in the official document, plain arithmetic, or an assumption that still needs confirming against the specification. The report never presents a guess as a requirement.
points: Wrote the rule engine and its checks for seller, buyer, header, line and total fields
Built loaders for flat CSV and Excel tables, and for formatted Excel invoices through a per-template cell map
Detected data damaged by spreadsheet software, such as a 15-digit tax number turned into scientific notation
Wrote the report generator and 53 unit tests

projects.title: AI Menu Integrator
projects.category: Menu digitisation SaaS for restaurants and POS systems
projects.summary: A multi-tenant service that takes a restaurant's menu as PDFs or photos and turns it into structured menu data a point-of-sale system can import.
projects.statusNote: Accounts, organisations, roles, restaurants and menu import are built: uploaded files are rendered page by page and their text is extracted, with OCR for scans. Turning that text into products and prices, the menu editor and the exports are not built yet.
overview: Restaurants keep their menus as PDFs and photos. Point-of-sale and delivery systems need them as structured data: items, prices and options. Retyping is slow and goes wrong.

The service is a modular monolith: a Next.js web app, a FastAPI service, PostgreSQL as both the database and the task queue, and separate worker processes for document handling. Every record is isolated per organisation with row-level security.

Today it gets as far as every page of every uploaded file rendered to an image, with its text extracted and positioned. Progress, per-page results, failures, retry and cancel are all visible in the app.
points: Built accounts, organisations, members and roles, and restaurants with locations
Built upload and menu import for PDF, PNG, JPEG and WebP files
Built the background worker that renders pages and extracts text, using the file's own text layer where there is one and OCR for scans
Isolated every organisation's data with row-level security
